components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Primary queue actions use dark ink and a compact rectangular silhouette.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #102731; color: #fcfdfa; padding: 0 14px; min-height: 39px; border: 1px solid #102731; border-radius: 8px; font: 500 12px/1.4 system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #1b3d49; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #f0a45b; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Answer Button
components.description: O/X choices show the code, action label, and evidence relationship.
components.css: .ds-btn-answer { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 48px 1fr; gap: 12px; align-items: center; min-height: 78px; padding: 14px 17px; border: 1px solid #102731; border-radius: 8px; color: #102731; background: transparent; } .ds-btn-answer:hover { color: #fcfdfa; background: #102731; transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-answer:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #f0a45b; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Search Field
components.description: Search fields stay plain and high-contrast so the query is easy to scan.
components.css: .ds-search { display: grid; gap: 7px; color: #334c52; font: 500 11px/1.4 monospace; } .ds-search input { height: 40px; padding: 0 12px; border: 1px solid #aab8b8; border-radius: 8px; color: #102731; background: #fcfdfa; } .ds-search input:focus { border-color: #086b64; outline: 3px solid #f0a45b; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Source Register
components.description: The evidence strip aligns source location and original excerpt after feedback.
components.css: .ds-register { padding: 15px 17px; border-top: 1px solid #aab8b8; background: #f0f3f1; color: #52666a; font: 500 11px/1.4 monospace; } .ds-register blockquote { margin: 12px 0 0; padding-left: 12px; border-left: 1px solid #086b64; color: #334c52; font: 400 12px/1.65 system-ui, sans-serif; }

narrative.overview:
The interface borrows the discipline of a print proof and an index card: cool paper, deep ink, narrow registration labels, and a single line that reveals where a claim came from. It is a working study desk first. Navigation, filters, buttons, and drawers remain recognisable web controls; the print language contributes only type, palette, density, and the registration-strip signature.

The page is intentionally calm and evidence-led. A learner should notice the sentence, choose O or X, then see the source location before chasing a score. The visual system uses tonal layering and thin rules rather than decorative texture or glow.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper surfaces with navy ink and restrained teal/coral state colors.
Monospace labels for source, location, counts, and other measurement-like metadata.
One-pixel registration marks that make evidence feel aligned, not ornamental.
Standard web interaction patterns with generous focus states and mobile reflow.

rules.name: The Register Rule
rules.body: Every answer state has a visible source register; correctness is never presented as an unexplained color flash.

dos: Do keep the statement readable before showing supporting metadata.
Do use teal and coral only for meaningful state or evidence signals.
Do keep source file names and locations visible at the moment of feedback.
Do preserve keyboard O/X/N shortcuts and visible focus.
donts: Don't turn the print reference into a fake paper notebook, ledger, or terminal costume.
Don't use color alone to communicate correct or wrong.
Don't add gradients, glow shadows, decorative grid overlays, or tiny functional labels.
Don't hide the public-source boundary when publishing the static site.
